name: Part-Of-Speech-Tagging
description: This dataset evaluates part-of-speech-based word extraction from English news sentences. Each example provides a raw sentence and a prompt asking to extract all words with specified adjective POS tags (JJ, JJR, JJS), and the target is a comma-separated list of the matching words.
card_text: The dataset contains 202 text-only examples drawn from news-style sentences, likely financial or general news. Each sample has an input object with a short raw text sentence and an instruction prompt that asks the model to identify all adjectives (POS tags JJ, JJR, JJS) in that sentence and return them as a comma-separated string. The output is a short list of extracted words. The task requires basic part-of-speech recognition and precise span extraction from context without any additional annotation. The data is monolingual English and uses a simple template-based prompting format.

context.semantics: The main input sentence is a short news-style statement that provides the text from which adjectives must be extracted. It is the source context for the extraction task.

question.semantics: The prompt is an explicit instruction that tells the model to extract words with adjective POS tags (JJ, JJR, JJS) from the raw_text and separate them with commas. It references the context via the <<<raw_text>>> placeholder.

answer.semantics: The target output is a comma-separated list of adjectives extracted from the context sentence, e.g. 'old, executive'. It directly answers the extraction instruction.

meta.meta_structure_description: Each sample consists of an input object and an output object. The input contains raw_text, a short news sentence serving as the context, and prompt, an instruction asking to extract adjective words from that context. The output contains text, a comma-separated list of the extracted adjectives. No other components such as options, dialogs, or visual data are present.
